In moderate to se- vere hepatic impairment, dosage of amsacrine may need to be reduced by up to 50%. Some licensed product information rec- ommends an initial reduction of 20 to 30%, to a dose between 60 and 75 mg/m2 daily. Administration in renal impairment. In moderate to severe renal impairment, dosage of amsacrine may need to be reduced by up to 50%. Some licensed product information recommends an initial reduction of 20 to 30%, to a dose between 60 and 75 mg/m2 daily. Adverse Effects, Treatment, and Precau- tions The most frequent adverse effects are gastrointestinal disturbances including anorexia, nausea and vomiting, and diarrhoea; asthenia; hot flushes; dizziness; drowsi- ness; headache; and rash. Other reported effects in- clude hair thinning, vaginal dryness or bleeding, myal- gia, arthralgia, and bone fractures, Abnormalities in liver enzyme values, thromboembolism, and increases in total cholesterol, have occurred in some patients re- ceiving anastrozole.
